[ W-SHARK // INTRO ]
02 / 10

Introduction | Making Posture Visible

Framing the necessity of low-impact, passive security auditing.

Modern web security requires continuous assessment of the visible surface area. While invasive penetration testing is critical, it often lacks the lightweight repeatability needed for baseline posture monitoring.

WeeShark bridges this gap by providing a deterministic, non-destructive audit engine that evaluates the defensive configuration of public-facing assets without service interruption.

Core Assessment Vectors

Transport Hygiene Evaluating TLS handshake validity and protocol version compliance.
Defensive Response Headers Validating CSP, HSTS, XFO, and XCTO configurations.
Privacy Controls Inspecting cookie attributes (Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite).
Exposure Management Detecting service banners and unauthorized port accessibility.
Source: WeeShark Technical Specification (2026)

files.title: literature.html
files.content:
[ W-SHARK // LIT-REV ]
03 / 10

Literature Review | Research Foundations

Synthesizing empirical studies and industry security standards.

Empirical Adoption

Analysis of the Adoption of Security Headers in HTTP

Buchanan et al. (2018) established the critical adoption gap in Top 1M sites. Found that despite low complexity, essential headers like HSTS and CSP were neglected by a majority of highly-trafficked endpoints.
Transport Standards

NIST SP 800-52 Rev. 2: TLS Guidelines

Standardizes the transition to TLS 1.2 and 1.3. Defines the necessity of FIPS-based cipher suites and certificate transparency as the baseline for trusted organizational communication.
Defensive Best Practice

OWASP SSRF & Headers Prevention Guides

Defines the zero-trust boundary for scanner implementations. Emphasizes DNS pre-resolution, private IP blocking, and redirection boundary enforcement as mandatory safeguards.

"The results show that, while implementation is increasing, it is still not implemented on many of the top sites... a distinct effort is required to achieve a passing grade." — Buchanan, IET Information Security (2018)

Sources: IET InfoSec (2018), NIST (2019), OWASP Cheat Sheets

files.title: problem.html
files.content:
[ W-SHARK // PROBLEM ]
04 / 10

Problem Statement | Baseline Without Overreach

Organizations lack an automated, low-friction mechanism to verify the defensive posture of their web assets against well-established standards without triggering aggressive security alerts or impacting availability.

Core Research Question

Can a passive audit engine effectively quantify web security posture using only non-destructive, externally visible signals while maintaining strict SSRF safety?

Assessment Scope

Evaluating encryption validity, header compliance, and service exposure. Excludes credential testing, application logic flaws, or invasive payloads.

Primary Objective

Standardize a weighted 0-100 scoring model grounded in NIST and OWASP guidance to prioritize remediation efforts across large asset pools.

Safety Constraint

Implement a multi-tier defense-in-depth boundary to ensure the assessment engine cannot be leveraged for Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF).

Project Goal: Continuous Posture Awareness

files.title: methodology.html
files.content:
[ W-SHARK // METHOD ]
05 / 10

Research Methodology | A Deterministic Audit Pipeline

Documenting the end-to-end execution flow of a passive assessment.

01

Ingest & Sanitize

Input normalization and protocol strictness enforcement (HTTP/S only).

02

SSRF Gate

DNS pre-resolution and multi-tier IP boundary validation.

03

Bounded Probe

Concurrent, non-destructive TLS, HTTP, and socket verification.

04

Score & Advise

Weighted quantification and remediation guidance generation.

05

Persist

Commit to SQLite ledger and hydration for reporting.

Protocol Gate: Only http:// and https:// schemes are accepted.
Network Safety: 1.2s socket timeouts to prevent hanging probes.
SSRF Boundary: DNS resolving prior to any outbound connection attempt.
Automation: Parallelized execution for real-time responsiveness.
Methodology: Automated Passive Assessment

files.title: scoring.html
files.content:
[ W-SHARK // SCORING ]
07 / 10

Measurement Model | Five Signals, One Score

A weighted quantification of visible security controls.

Assessment Vector Criteria Max Pts
HTTPS Encryption TLS Handshake + Protocol Validity 25
Security Headers CSP, HSTS, XFO, XCTO Presence 35
Cookie Attributes Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite Flags 15
Info Disclosure Software Banner Suppression 10
Port Hygiene Unauthorized Service Exposure 15

Risk Classifications

EXCELLENT (90-100)
Robust defensive configuration.
GOOD (75-89)
Solid baseline; minor gaps.
MEDIUM (50-74)
Missing critical headers or flags.
CRITICAL (0-49)
Significant unencrypted exposure.
Metric Calibration: Grounded in NIST/OWASP guidance.

[ W-SHARK // RESULTS ]
08 / 10

Results & Discussion | Project Verification

Evaluating implementation completeness against documented test evidence.

Test Coverage Distribution

SSRF Protection Performance

Logic Verification Validated 42+ Python unit tests covering SSRF, URL normalization, and scoring logic. 100% pass rate in CI environment.
API Integrity Express API tests confirm input sanitization and RCE protection on scan ID lookups.
Evidence Gap Current results are benchmarked against simulated targets; large-scale real-world empirical validation remains a future phase.
Data Source: Internal Project Test Logs (2026)

files.title: conclusion.html
files.content:
[ W-SHARK // CONCL ]
09 / 10

Conclusion & Future Scope

Summarizing the contribution to passive security auditing.

Key Contributions

Deterministic Posture Quantification Establishing a repeatable baseline across five assessment vectors.
Hardened Safety Boundary Multi-tier SSRF prevention ensures authorized-only defensive use.
Accessible Remediation Actionable recommendations translated from raw header/TLS signals.

Future Research

Large-Scale Empirical Validation Scanning Top 1M domains to benchmark the WeeShark scoring model.
Extended Service Fingerprinting Detecting a broader range of exposed administrative interfaces.
Trend Analysis over Time Historical tracking of posture drift within organizational assets.
Continuous Improvement in Defensive Security

⚠️ Responsible Use Warning
WeeShark is designed for authorized defensive audits only. Performing network scans or port probes against third-party systems without explicit written consent may violate cybersecurity laws and regulations. Users are responsible for ensuring all assessment targets are within their authorized scope.
